newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen steady to slightly lower at open.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen steady to slightly lower at open.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to open steady to slightly lower on Friday, taking their cues from the bond market following a stronger-than-forecast rise in June durable goods orders data.

"We could see a replay of yesterday, with early pressure to bonds and stocks," Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities, said. "But how we open is completely immaterial to how we close, with each day a journey unto its own."
Durable goods orders rose 2.3 percent in June compared to a forecast rise of 1.4 percent. May data was revised to a decline of 0.4 percent from a 0.7 percent drop.

"The data put initial pressure on the bond market and that could continue in the session," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "We could see some profit-taking in the stocks if we have a weak bond market."
But analysts said durable goods data tended to be volatile, and financial markets took this into account.

"It's a tricky figure," Wachtel said. "Transportation orders are included in durable goods -- big ticket items like airplane orders and rails...If you exclude transportation, orders rose a more normal 0.5 percent."
